diagnosis.root_cause: Not confirmed. I traced the whole retrieval path and none of the code I read would return wrong or unrelated chunks. The /retrieve endpoint (patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py) embeds the question and queries ChromaDB with the requested top_k. The embedder (patient/ingestion_service/app/embedder.py) calls the Ollama embedding endpoint and counts every hash-fallback use. The incident's embedding_fallbacks_per_min=0 therefore suggests real embeddings were returned. The vector store (patient/ingestion_service/app/vector_store.py) uses a cosine collection, reports similarity as 1 - distance and keeps Chroma's ranking order, with no reversal or filtering. One lead I could not verify: QueryRequest.collection_name defaults to "default" (main.py:29), while the vector store's own default is "knowledge_base" (vector_store.py:32). get_or_create_collection silently creates an empty collection, so a caller that leaves out collection_name would get no chunks and no error. That would usually show up in the zero-chunk-retrieval metric, which the incident report does not mention. I did not read the gateway's call or diff deploys 6cd5503 and 4e34716 against 70c3dff, so I cannot name a defect or a commit. The doctor's second hypothesis (Ollama generation saturation near the 120 s timeout) is a capacity cause that no code change would fix, and it is also still open. Recommended next steps before patching anything: diff the retrieval service across the two deploys, check which collection_name the gateway sends, and run known evaluation questions through /retrieve.
evidence: patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py:73-80 - the query is embedded with instrumented_embedding and passed to query_vector_store with req.collection_name and req.top_k. No reranking or filtering happens.
patient/ingestion_service/app/vector_store.py:32-37 - get_or_create_collection defaults to "knowledge_base" and silently creates any collection that is missing.
patient/ingestion_service/app/vector_store.py:98-136 - top_k is min(top_k, count), results keep Chroma's order and similarity = 1 - cosine distance. This is correct.
patient/ingestion_service/app/embedder.py:26-32,70-73 - every hash fallback increments _FALLBACK_COUNT, so a fallback rate of 0 means real embeddings were used.
patient/common/telemetry.py:142-157 - instrumented_embedding only times the call and counts fallbacks. Behaviour is unchanged.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py b/patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py
--- a/patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py
+++ b/patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py
@@ -26,7 +26,7 @@
 
 class QueryRequest(BaseModel):
     question: str
-    collection_name: str = "default"
+    collection_name: str = "knowledge_base"
     top_k: int = 4
     embedding_model: str = "nomic-embed-text"
     ollama_base_url: str = Field(default_factory=config.ollama_base_url)
patch.rationale:
The previous attempt returned no edits, so it failed validation. This attempt changes one line, but the cause is still unconfirmed.

The only concrete inconsistency in the retrieval path is a collection-name mismatch. QueryRequest.collection_name defaults to "default", but the vector store reads and writes "knowledge_base" by default (get_or_create_collection). Any /retrieve caller that leaves out collection_name therefore queries a different, silently created empty collection. query_vector_store returns [] for an empty collection. assemble_context then sends "No relevant document chunks found." as the context, and the LLM answers without grounding. That gives wrong or unrelated answers with no errors, no restarts and no embedding fallbacks.

Two incident signals fit this cause:
- Retrieval memory fell to a flat ~104 MB. An empty collection never loads the HNSW index.
- The answers stayed silent: no errors were raised.

The patch aligns the request default with the vector store default, so callers that leave out collection_name search the collection that ingestion actually populates. Explicit collection_name values, including the one the evaluation harness passes, are unaffected.

I have not confirmed this is the cause:
- The gateway payload was not inspected.
- The diffs for 6cd5503 and 4e34716 were not available.
- The zero-chunk-retrieval metric was not reported in the incident.

Operators should still diff the deploys, check the zero-chunk counter and run known evaluation questions through /retrieve. If this fix does not restore relevance, roll back retrieval. Ollama generation saturation remains a separate capacity issue.
